Reason: Recurrent vomiting and diarrhea with blood streaks for 24 hours, accompanied by lethargy and anorexia.
Skin_and_Coat: Dull coat, slightly decreased skin turgor, no visible ectoparasites.
Eyes_and_Ears: Normochromic sclerae, preserved pupillary light reflex, clean ear canals.
Cardiovascular: Rhythmic heart sounds without murmurs, symmetrical femoral pulses, CRT 2.5 seconds.
Respiratory: Clear lung fields on bilateral auscultation, no adventitious sounds.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Pain on deep abdominal palpation in the epigastric region, hyperactive bowel sounds.
Musculoskeletal: Coordinated gait without lameness, spinous processes and joints non-painful on palpation.
Neurological: Alert, responsive to environmental stimuli, normal cranial nerves and spinal reflexes.
Urinary_or_Genital: Normotypic descended testicles, moderately full bladder with soft wall.
Anamnesis: Accidental ingestion of organic trash 48 hours ago. Presents repeated bilious vomiting and dark, watery stool.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Acute hemorrhagic gastroenteritis secondary to dietary indiscretion.
Treatment: IV Lactated Ringer's solution (50 mL/kg/day), Maropitant 1 mg/kg SC q24h, Ondansetron 0.5 mg/kg IV q12h, Metronidazole 10 mg/kg IV q12h.
Clarification_Notes: Patient shows significant clinical improvement; resolution of vomiting and good tolerance to gradual oral rehydration.

Reason: Severe pruritus, erythema, and hair loss in ventral region, axillae, and pinnae lasting 2 weeks.
Skin_and_Coat: Diffuse erythema, lichenification, and hyperpigmentation in axillary and ventral areas with excoriations from scratching.
Eyes_and_Ears: Erythematous ear pinnae with bilateral abundant brownish ceruminous exudate.
Cardiovascular: Regular heart rate, normal sound intensity, absence of murmurs, CRT < 2 seconds.
Respiratory: Normal respiratory rate and pattern, lung fields clear to auscultation.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Abdomen soft, non-tender to palpation, no detectable organomegaly.
Musculoskeletal: Symmetrical weight-bearing, full and painless joint range of motion.
Neurological: Alert mental status, oriented to surroundings, preserved cranial reflexes.
Urinary_or_Genital: Normal vulvar conformation without exudate or inflammatory signs.
Anamnesis: Compulsive pruritus rated 8/10 for 14 days. Constant licking of interdigital spaces. Fed a regular commercial diet.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Canine atopic dermatitis complicated by secondary pyoderma and Malassezia otitis externa.
Treatment: Prednisolone 0.5 mg/kg PO q24h for 5 days then q48h for 5 days; Chlorhexidine 3% / Ketoconazole 2% shampoo baths q7d; Posaconazole/Florfenicol otic drops q24h for 7 days.
Clarification_Notes: Follow-up phone call: 60% reduction in pruritus, no gastrointestinal side effects reported.

Reason: Intermittent left hindlimb lameness and skipping gait when trotting.
Skin_and_Coat: Good coat condition, no ectoparasites, adequate skin turgor.
Eyes_and_Ears: Ocular globes free of discharge, normal photomotor reflexes, clean ears.
Cardiovascular: Cardiac auscultation within normal limits, pulses symmetrical and synchronous.
Respiratory: Mildly positive tracheal sensitivity, physiological vesicular breath sounds bilaterally.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Soft abdomen, no evidence of pain or masses on abdominal palpation.
Musculoskeletal: Grade II medial patellar luxation on left hindlimb, manually reducible. Mild discomfort on left stifle flexion.
Neurological: Proprioception intact in all four limbs, no focal neurological deficits.
Urinary_or_Genital: Normal external genitalia, both testes descended within the scrotum.
Anamnesis: Owner noticed a 'skipping' gait on the left hindlimb for the past 3 days after jumping off the couch. No major traumatic event reported.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Grade II medial patellar luxation of the left hindlimb.
Treatment: Meloxicam 0.1 mg/kg PO q24h for 5 days, joint supplement (glucosamine/chondroitin) PO q24h, strict restriction from jumping for 14 days.
Clarification_Notes: More consistent weight-bearing on the limb; noticeable reduction in skipping episodes.

Reason: Paroxysmal dry hacking cough, retching, and expectoration of white foam following exercise or excitement.
Skin_and_Coat: Dense, clean coat, preserved skin elasticity, free of ectoparasites.
Eyes_and_Ears: Mild bilateral clear epiphora, normal external auditory canals.
Cardiovascular: Heart rate age-appropriate, clear sounds without murmurs, CRT 1.5 seconds.
Respiratory: Tracheal pinch reflex strongly positive (+3/3), triggering a dry paroxysmal cough. Bilateral harsh inspiratory sounds on thoracic auscultation.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Abdomen soft on palpation, no pain or intestinal distension.
Musculoskeletal: Symmetrical muscle development for age, smooth and painless locomotion.
Neurological: Puppy is bright, alert, and responsive with normal reflexes.
Urinary_or_Genital: Both testes fully descended into the scrotum, normal prepuce and micturition without discharge.
Anamnesis: Acquired from breeder 5 days ago. Developed a dry, honking cough when excited. Apetite and activity remain high.
Treatment: Doxycycline 10 mg/kg PO q24h for 10 days, Meloxicam 0.05 mg/kg PO q24h for 3 days, 0.9% saline nebulization q12h.
Clarification_Notes: Decreased severity of coughing fits; puppy remains active and eating well.

Reason: Frequent watery vomiting, acute abdominal pain, anorexia, and 'prayer position' posture for 12 hours.
Skin_and_Coat: Dull coat, reduced skin elasticity (skin tent duration 3 seconds).
Eyes_and_Ears: Mild conjunctival injection, normal pupillary light reflexes, clean ears.
Cardiovascular: Sinus tachycardia secondary to pain, full femoral pulses, CRT 3 seconds.
Respiratory: Tachypneic breathing secondary to abdominal discomfort, lungs clear without rales.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Marked pain response to deep palpation in the epigastrium and cranial right quadrant with abdominal guarding.
Musculoskeletal: Antalgic 'prayer position' posture with raised hindquarters, normal joint range of motion.
Neurological: Lethargic mental state, reduced response to surroundings but responsive to clinical handling.
Urinary_or_Genital: Normotypic external genitalia, concentrated urine of reduced volume.
Anamnesis: Ingested a large quantity of high-fat food during a family event the previous evening. Rapid onset of severe emesis and complete anorexia.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Acute pancreatitis secondary to high-fat dietary indiscretion.
Treatment: Inpatient hospitalization, IV fluid therapy with supplemented Lactated Ringer's, Tramadol 3 mg/kg IV q8h, Maropitant 1 mg/kg IV q24h, Omeprazole 1 mg/kg IV q24h.
Clarification_Notes: Inpatient monitoring; abdominal pain reduced to mild/moderate (2/10), no emetic episodes in the last 12h. Positive SNAP cPL test.

Reason: Dysuria, stranguria, gross hematuria, and frequent licking of the prepuce.
Skin_and_Coat: Spotted coat with good density and no ectoparasites, normal skin turgor.
Eyes_and_Ears: Ocular and auditory structures within physiological parameters.
Cardiovascular: Normal heart rate and rhythm, clean auscultation, CRT < 2 seconds.
Respiratory: Normal costoabdominal respiratory pattern, lung auscultation unremarkable.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Caudal abdomen tense, bladder distended and tender to palpation.
Musculoskeletal: Coordinated gait, slight discomfort when assuming posturing for urinating.
Neurological: Alert, responsive, and oriented, normal cranial nerves and spinal reflexes.
Urinary_or_Genital: Prepuce congested, difficult passage of urine containing bloody streaks and microcrystals.
Anamnesis: Owner observed frequent posture to urinate, producing only drops of bloody urine for the past 24 hours. High animal-protein diet.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Urocystolithiasis (ammonium urate uroliths) and secondary cystitis.
Treatment: Urethral catheterization and bladder lavage under sedation, Enrofloxacin 10 mg/kg PO q24h for 10 days, Meloxicam 0.1 mg/kg PO q24h for 5 days, Allopurinol 10 mg/kg PO q12h, transition to low-purine diet.
Clarification_Notes: Urination restored to steady stream and clearer color following urinary catheter removal; drinking water normally.

Reason: Prostration, severe weakness, continuous vomiting, and foul-smelling bloody diarrhea for 36 hours.
Skin_and_Coat: Dull coat, persistent skin tenting (>4 seconds), cool extremities to touch.
Eyes_and_Ears: Markedly sunken eyes (enophthalmos), pale conjunctivae, reflexes intact.
Cardiovascular: Severe tachycardia, weak and thready femoral pulses, CRT 3.5 seconds.
Respiratory: Compensatory polypnea due to metabolic acidosis, lung fields clear on auscultation.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Severe diffuse abdominal pain on palpation, thickened intestinal loops filled with fluid and gas.
Musculoskeletal: Generalized muscle weakness and inability to stand for prolonged periods.
Neurological: Lethargic/stuporous mental state, moderate response to auditory and painful stimuli.
Urinary_or_Genital: Clean vulva without discharge, oliguria secondary to severe dehydration.
Anamnesis: Recently acquired puppy with incomplete vaccination history (only 1 dose). Febrile onset, persistent vomiting, and profuse hemorrhagic diarrhea.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Canine Parvovirus enteritis (CPV-2) confirmed by rapid antigen test.
Treatment: Isolation ICU admission, intensive IV fluid therapy with Lactated Ringer's + 2.5% Dextrose, Cefazolin 22 mg/kg IV q8h, Maropitant 1 mg/kg IV q24h, Buprenorphine 0.01 mg/kg IV q8h.
Clarification_Notes: Patient stable under continuous ICU monitoring; gradual reduction in vomiting (1 episode in 24 hours).

Reason: Frequent paroxysmal sneezing, mucopurulent nasal discharge, bilateral ocular epiphora, and lethargy.
Skin_and_Coat: Unkempt coat due to reduced self-grooming, slightly decreased skin turgor, presence of small focal erosions on the nasal planum.
Eyes_and_Ears: Mild blepharospasm, bilateral seromucous ocular discharge, fluorescein stain negative.
Cardiovascular: Clear cardiac sounds, no gallop rhythm or murmurs, CRT 2 seconds.
Respiratory: Bilateral mucopurulent nasal discharge, moist upper airway rales, lower lungs clear.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Soft abdomen on palpation, no pain or organomegaly.
Musculoskeletal: Intact musculoskeletal structure, no joint pain or swelling.
Neurological: Alert, depressed due to respiratory congestion, normal spinal reflexes.
Urinary_or_Genital: Testes descended into scrotum, normal urinary function.
Anamnesis: Cat with outdoor access. Sneezing started 4 days ago progressing to nasal and ocular discharge, with hyporexia due to loss of smell.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Feline Respiratory Disease Complex (Feline Herpesvirus-1 / Feline Calicivirus).
Treatment: Doxycycline oral liquid suspension 10 mg/kg PO q24h for 14 days, Meloxicam 0.05 mg/kg PO q24h for 3 days, saline nebulizations and Tobramycin eye drops q8h.
Clarification_Notes: Favorable progress: reduced nasal congestion and recovery of appetite with warmed wet food.

Reason: Dysuria, painful vocalization when attempting to urinate in litter box, periuria, and hematuria.
Skin_and_Coat: Glossy, well-groomed coat, no evidence of ectoparasites.
Eyes_and_Ears: Normal ocular globes, symmetrical and normoreactive photomotor reflexes.
Cardiovascular: Regular cardiac rhythm, auscultation free of murmurs or gallop, CRT < 2 seconds.
Respiratory: Respiratory rate and pattern within physiological limits.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Tense caudal abdomen with pain response to palpation. Moderately firm bladder.
Musculoskeletal: Normal mobility, no manifested joint pain or lameness.
Neurological: Attentive, restless due to urinary discomfort, reflexes intact.
Urinary_or_Genital: Mildly congested penis; cloudy urine with abundant red blood cells and struvite crystals.
Anamnesis: Recent environmental stress from moving home. Started 24 hours ago repeatedly visiting litter box with painful vocalizations and passing small amounts of blood-tinged urine.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Non-obstructive Feline Idiopathic Cystitis (FIC) and struvite crystalluria.
Treatment: Buprenorphine 0.02 mg/kg transmucosal q8h for 3 days, Prazosin 0.5 mg PO q12h for 5 days, transition to wet Urinary S/O diet and Feliway Classic diffuser.
Clarification_Notes: Patient passing larger urine volumes without vocalizing. Marked reduction in anxiety.

Reason: Marked abdominal distension ('pot-bellied' appearance), soft diarrhea with visible helminthes, dull coat, and lethargy.
Skin_and_Coat: Dull, unkempt, and dry coat; sparse subcutaneous fat.
Eyes_and_Ears: Pale conjunctivae, external ear canals free of parasites.
Cardiovascular: Normophonic heart sounds, appropriate rate for a kitten, CRT 2 seconds.
Respiratory: Lung fields clear bilaterally, no adventitious sounds.
Digestive_or_ Abdomen: Markedly distended pot-bellied abdomen, audible borborygmi, discomfort on deep palpation.
Musculoskeletal: Reduced muscle mass for age, bone structure intact without deformities.
Neurological: Kitten is alert and curious, but fatigues quickly.
Anamnesis: Rescued kitten with no prior deworming history. Presents continuous loose stools with spontaneous passage of roundworms.
Presumptive_Diagnosis: Severe gastrointestinal parasitism (Toxocara cati and Giardia lamblia).
Treatment: Fenbendazole 50 mg/kg PO q24h for 5 days, feline digestive probiotics q24h, repeat Fenbendazole dose in 14 days.
Clarification_Notes: Massive passage of parasites in stool; stool consistency improving and increased appetite.
